I've been working this land for 20 years. My land here in Quzhou is flat, irrigation is reliable from the well, and I know what works. My children help some but also work in town, so I can't spend as much time on the fields as I used to. I need to keep things manageable.

My 16.1 mu splits naturally: about 12 mu runs the wheat-maize rotation — that's my stable income, I can predict it. The remaining 4.1 mu I put in cotton — it earns more per mu when the market is good, but it's labor-heavy, so I don't push it bigger.

**Wheat (winter, ~12 mu):** I'll use the improved Jimai variety the county extension people promoted a few years back — better yield than what my father planted. I rotary-till before seeding in early October. I apply compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, then urea at jointing. Four irrigations: pre-sowing to get the seedbed right, one in winter to protect roots from cold, jointing, and heading. Two pesticide passes — herbicide early winter, then mixed fungicide and aphid spray in April.

**Maize (summer, ~12 mu):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed hybrid seed (Zhengdan 958, reliable). No-till saves me time and fuel when I'm busy. Most rain falls in July-August so irrigation is lighter — I watch it and irrigate twice unless it rains enough. Fertilizer goes as base plus topdressing at tasseling. Two pesticide applications for borer and leaf blight.

**Cotton (spring/summer, ~4.1 mu):** Cotton takes the most watching. I rotary-till in April, transplant seedlings in early May. Five pesticide passes — bollworm is the real problem here. Three irrigations at boll-setting stages. I use an improved variety, not hybrid cotton, because the seeds are cheaper and I save some from last year.

I'm not changing much from last year. What I do works well enough, and at my age I'm not going to experiment with the whole farm.
